text:
Alex: seeing a sudden jump in NCCL watchdog timeouts + Xid errors on multiple GPUs in us-east after the driver rollout. graphs: https://grafana.redwood/.. :eyes:
infra-bot: Alert (severity=high) forwarded to #eng-sre and INC-2026-314 created
Sam: which nodepool? any pattern by instance type or kernel?
Alex: us-east-gpu-pool-1, mostly A10s + a few H100s. errors start ~10:03 UTC. No obvious memory OOM.
Maria: pulling logs now — running `kubectl logs -l role=gpu -n inference --since=30m | grep -i "Xid\|watchdog"`
Cheng: we did a kernel bump on the canary subset last night (6.1.12). driver roll started this morning (535.23).
Maria: canary nodes are showing identical `NCCL WARN Watchdog` entries, Xid 31 and sporadic Xid 43.
Sam: sounds like regression between driver+kernel combo. Recommend pause rollout and cordon the canary nodes.
Alex: pausing rollout now in the deploy system — routing flagged at 10:07 UTC.\nAlex: note: fallback routing to us-west will add ~25-40% p90 latency; capacity there is limited.
Maria: quick checks: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,driver_version,utilization.gpu --format=csv` -> driver 535.23 on affected, util spikes before watchdog events.
Cheng: could be NIC/GSO/MTU interplay causing long tail kernel scheduling + driver kernel calls. Any MTU changes in the past 48h?
Sam: I saw a config change on lb-us-east-1 last night that lowered MTU to 1400 for an experiment. Putting that on the list to correlate.
Maria: capturing dmesg + kernel logs from affected nodes and uploading: s3://redwood-ops/tmp/1798765432-dmesg.tar.gz
infra-bot: Runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/nccl-watchdog — recommended steps: cordon/drain, capture logs, revert driver/kernel on canary, open vendor ticket.
Alex: Action plan (short): 1) pause driver rollout (done) 2) cordon & drain canary nodes 3) revert kernel on canary to 5.15 4) throttle new batch rollouts 5) open vendor ticket with logs + reproducer 6) consider partial traffic shift to us-west 7) run extended canary after fix
Cheng: I'll assemble rollback playbook and test in staging. will also include kernel+driver matrix test harness (small MLP and NCCL allreduce).
Maria: starting cordon/drain now: `kubectl cordon gpu-canary-01 && kubectl drain gpu-canary-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Sam: I'll coordinate capacity in us-west with cloud team and estimate cost of burst GPUs (ETA 15m).
Alex: keep notes on cost impact — we may need to flag finance if we spin up >48h extra capacity.
Maria: collecting KV cache stats and token throughput to check for batching effects that could exacerbate timeouts.
Cheng: pinging vendor support with collected bundles. request id: VEND-8792.
Alex: once we have vendor ack, we'll decide rollback vs patch. For now keep rollout paused and no further driver promotions.
Sam: ack. I'll update the incident and post a short summary to #all-hands if this impacts customer SLAs.
Maria: any quick mitigations? reconfiguring MTU back to 1500 on the LB helps in canary reenactment. testing now.
Alex: update 10:34 UTC — MTU revert on one canary reduced watchdogs by ~60% in the short window. Not full fix.
Cheng: good signal. I'll prioritize kernel rollback + run full NCCL test matrix in staging, then safe rollback in canary at 20% traffic.
Maria: attaching logs and a short reproducer script in the incident ticket.
infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-314 updated: status=investigating, priority=P1
Alex: thanks team. keep updates concise in this thread. we'll reconvene in 30m for next steps. :thumbsup:
